figures.title: Annual revenue by company
figures.description: A spreadsheet-friendly grouped column chart summarizing yearly revenue.

figures.title: Quarterly revenue trend
figures.description: An interactive Plotly time series showing quarterly revenue movement.

figures.title: Indexed revenue growth
figures.description: A normalized view that compares each company's growth from its Q1 2020 baseline.

figures.title: The $2.64B streaming turnaround was overwhelmingly revenue-driven
figures.description: Board view of the operating drivers behind Disney Direct-to-Consumer's improvement in operating income.
figures.takeaway: Revenue growth contributed $2.89B of improvement, partially offset by $406M of higher SG&A.

figures.title: Legacy TV still earns more — but streaming crossed the line into profit
figures.description: Investor view comparing 2023 and 2024 operating income for Linear Networks and Direct-to-Consumer.
figures.takeaway: Linear Networks lost $667M of operating income while DTC improved by $2.64B and became profitable.

figures.title: Streaming's margin gap remains 31.7 points behind Linear Networks
figures.description: Board view benchmarking 2023 and 2024 operating margins for streaming and Linear Networks.
figures.takeaway: DTC improved 13.2 points to a 0.6% margin, but Linear Networks still earned a 32.3% margin in 2024.

figures.title: Streaming became the majority of Entertainment revenue
figures.description: Investor view of the shift in Entertainment revenue mix toward Direct-to-Consumer.
figures.takeaway: DTC rose from 48.9% to 55.3% of Entertainment revenue in one year.

dashboard.headline: Disney's streaming transition, organized by financial insight and audience.
dashboard.summary: Each insight below is presented twice: first for the board of directors, then for potential investors. The financial data is the same, but the chart design and level of detail change with the decision context.

groups.label: Insight A
groups.title: Streaming moved from a major loss to profitability while Linear Networks declined.
groups.description: DTC operating income improved by $2.64B, from a $2.50B loss to a $143M profit, while Linear Networks operating income fell $667M. The board view explains what drove the turnaround; the investor view emphasizes the strategic shift.

groups.label: Insight B
groups.title: Streaming became the majority of Entertainment revenue, but its margins remain far below traditional TV.
groups.description: DTC increased from 48.9% to 55.3% of Entertainment revenue and its operating margin improved from -12.6% to +0.6%. The board view benchmarks the remaining 31.7-point margin gap; the investor view focuses on the change in revenue mix.

figures.title: Where the $491.7K sits: a tech-heavy, equity-dominated mix
figures.description: Portfolio market value broken down by sector and then by individual holding.
figures.takeaway: Technology (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA) is the largest sector, and individual stocks outweigh the diversifying funds.

figures.title: Technology is the largest concentration at 26% of assets
figures.description: Each sector's share of total portfolio value, ranked to surface concentration.
figures.takeaway: No single sector besides Technology exceeds 10%, but the tech tilt drives both the portfolio's upside and its volatility.

figures.title: The portfolio gained $39.9K — but the result is highly uneven
figures.description: A waterfall from total cost basis to current value, with each holding's dollar contribution.
figures.takeaway: VTI, NVDA, and MSFT drove most of the gain, while AMZN and BND together erased nearly $29K.

figures.title: Longer-held and well-timed positions delivered the biggest returns
figures.description: Each holding's total return since purchase, plotted against its purchase date and sized by current value.
figures.takeaway: Positions bought in 2020-2021 (VTI, MSFT) generally outperformed; AMZN is the clear outlier despite an early entry.

figures.title: Risk and reward: NVIDIA is the high-risk, high-return corner
figures.description: Annualized volatility versus total return, sized by position value, against portfolio averages.
figures.takeaway: BND anchors the low-risk corner, NVDA/VTI reward their risk, and AMZN carries high volatility with a deep loss.

figures.title: Which positions punch above their weight in risk
figures.description: Each holding's share of invested capital compared with its share of portfolio risk (weight × volatility).
figures.takeaway: NVDA, AMZN, and XOM contribute more risk than capital, while BND and PG dampen it.

dashboard.eyebrow: Balanced Growth Portfolio · As of December 31, 2024
dashboard.headline: A tech-tilted growth portfolio: where the money sits, how it performed, and where the risk hides.
dashboard.summary: Fourteen holdings worth $491,650 are examined through three lenses — asset allocation, performance, and risk. The same portfolio is read three ways so that composition, returns, and risk concentration can each be judged on their own terms.

groups.label: Asset allocation
groups.title: Equities dominate, and Technology is the single largest bet.
groups.description: The treemap maps every position by market value; the ranked bar isolates sector weights and flags the portfolio's concentration in Technology.

groups.label: Performance over time
groups.title: A few winners carried the portfolio; entry timing explains much of the spread.
groups.description: The bridge decomposes each holding's contribution to total profit and loss; the scatter relates each position's return to when it was purchased.

groups.label: Risk analysis
groups.title: High-volatility positions carry more risk than their size suggests.
groups.description: The risk-return scatter locates every holding against portfolio averages; the contribution bars compare each position's share of capital with its share of portfolio risk.
